headline_marked: FIFA confirms [[Bangladesh's participation in ASEAN Cup]]
headline: FIFA confirms Bangladesh's participation in ASEAN Cup
summary: The national team will replace India in the tournament scheduled for September 24 to October 4 in Jakarta, Indonesia.
details: FIFA has officially confirmed that Bangladesh will participate in the FIFA ASEAN Cup in Jakarta, Indonesia, from September 24 to October 4.
The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) confirmed the news following an executive committee meeting on Saturday, stating they had received a positive response from FIFA.
Bangladesh enters the tournament as a last-minute replacement for India, who withdrew due to clashes with other international assignments.
The national team will be placed in Group A, where they will face hosts Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore.
Group B consists of Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, and Pakistan.
The BFF has announced that a national team camp will be called very soon, following discussions with head coach Thomas Dooley.
caption:
Bangladesh is heading to Jakarta! 🇧🇩

FIFA has confirmed the national team's spot in the ASEAN Cup.

FIFA has officially confirmed that Bangladesh will participate in the FIFA ASEAN Cup in Jakarta, Indonesia, from September 24 to October 4.

The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) confirmed the news following an executive committee meeting on Saturday, stating they had received a positive response from FIFA.

Bangladesh enters the tournament as a last-minute replacement for India, who withdrew due to clashes with other international assignments.

The national team will be placed in Group A, where they will face hosts Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore.

Group B consists of Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, and Pakistan.

The BFF has announced that a national team camp will be called very soon, following discussions with head coach Thomas Dooley.

#Bangladesh #Football #FIFAASEANCup #BFF #Jakarta

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Home Minister warns [[action against law enforcers]] if extortionists aren't caught
headline: Home Minister warns action against law enforcers if extortionists aren't caught
summary: Minister Salahuddin Ahmed says police members involved in extortion rings will be listed and penalized if they fail to stop organized crime targeting professionals.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has ordered the immediate arrest of identified extortionists, terrorists, and drug dealers. He warned that law enforcement officers who fail to bring these criminals into custody will face disciplinary action.

The warning came during a visit to Professor Asadur Rahman, the head of the ENT department at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, who was recently attacked. The professor had previously received extortion demands of $15,000 in the name of a top terrorist from Chittagong.

Police have already arrested four people in connection with the attack on the professor, including one from Lakshmipur and two from Dhaka. The Minister noted that an organized gang is targeting wealthy individuals, doctors, and engineers through threatening messages.

Minister Ahmed stated that the government is not only listing extortionists but is also identifying police officers involved in these criminal rings. He emphasized that the goal is to eradicate organized extortion networks that use the names of 'godfathers' to intimidate victims.

To enhance security for medical professionals, 10 Ansar members will be deployed to 500 hospitals across the country. The Minister also advised doctors who feel at risk in their private chambers or clinics to notify the police for special security.

Regarding personal safety, the Minister clarified that any citizen, including doctors, can apply for a shotgun or pistol license under existing laws. Applications from doctors seeking firearms for self-defense will be regarded with importance by the government.
